question.text: This economic and social campaign beginning in 1958 sought to rapidly transform China from an agrarian economy to modern communist society. It failed miserably.
question.clue: Millions of people were encouraged to set up backyard furnaces during this campaign.

swap.text: This is the total number of women who have ever been Supreme Court justices, past and present.
swap.clue: Jiang Qing, Mao's final wife, was a member of a group of this number of people. Sparrows were exterminated as part of a campaign against this number of pests.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese history.
question.text: This rebellion's leader, Hong Xiuquan, claimed to be the brother of Jesus, and it attempted to establish a "Heavenly Kingdom" in mid-nineteenth century China.
question.clue: The majority of those who participated belonged to the Hakka class, and soon after one of their armies was repulsed by Frederick Townsend Ward, their leader took poison and died in a sewer.

swap.text: The UK turned over control of this Special Administrative Region to China in 1997, two years beforePortugal did the same with nearby Macau.
swap.clue: A series of protests in this city was named after the umbrellas used to shield demonstrators from police tear gas.

question.leadin: The rival philosophies of Daoism and Legalism emerged during the collapse of this dynasty, which won the Battle of Muye.
question.text: Name this dynasty which oversaw the flourishing of the Hundred Schools of Thought during the Spring and Autumn Period.
question.clue: The Hundred Schools flourished during the Eastern part of the dynasty, whose rulers were the first to claim the (* ) Mandate of Heaven.

swap.leadin: This man was given his new surname by the Yongle emperor.
swap.text: Name this Muslim eunuch who was comissioned to go on seven "treasure voyages" in the oceans south of China, ranging all the way to Africa. His ships were the largest wooden ships ever built.
swap.clue: A controversial 2002 work by Gavin Menzies claimed that this man discovered the Americas, Australia, and the Northeast Passage.

question.leadin: One ruler of this dynasty ordered the completion of the Grand Canal, and may have ordered the murder of his father, Emperor Wen, who founded this dynasty.
question.text: Name this dynasty centered at Chang'an that was ruled by Emperor Yang and succeeded by the Tang and Song dynasties.
question.clue: The dynasty's last emperor, Yang, was the son of its first, Yang Chien, who took the royal name of Wen Ti.

swap.text: During the war, Chiang's Kuomintang forces chased the retreating communists all the way north to Shaanxi in this military campaign, during which Mao Zedong came to power.
swap.clue: The Fifth Encirclement forced this event, which Otto Braun took part in. The participants of this event defeated warlord forces at the Battle of Luding Bridge and reshuffled their leadership at the Zunyi Conference.

question.text: Admiral Makarov was killed at this eleven-month battle that took place at modern Lushun. For 15 points, Maresuke Nogi was able to win what land engagement of the Russo-Japanese War due to Admiral Togo's sea support?
question.clue: The British spy Sidney Reilly allegedly stole defense plans to a military base in this city commanded by Oskar Stark.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about China's last emperor, P'u Yi.
swap.text: P'u Yi lived his young life in this complex, not leaving until he was forced to in 1924. Aside from royals, the only males allowed in the inner palace were court eunuchs.
swap.clue: The earth removed in the construction of the moat around this place was used to create Jingshan Hill, the place where the Chongzhen Emperor committed suicide.

question.leadin: The yin privilege allowed high ranking bureaucrats to place their sons into low positions of power without having to deal with this system.
question.text: Name this system, success in which allowed scholar-bureaucrats to advance by demonstrating knowledge of wenxue. The challenging Eight-legged essay was an integral part of this system.
question.answerHtml: Chinese imperial examinations [accept equivalents like the Chinese civil service exams]

swap.text: The Nihon Shoki attributes the introduction of Chinese characters to Japan to a state in a Korean period with this name. Cao Cao's exploits are featured in a Chinese novel named for this period.
swap.answerHtml: Three Kingdoms [accept Three Kingdoms of Korea or Samhan of Korea; accept Sānguó Shídài; accept Romance of the Three Kingdoms or Sānguó Yanyì]
swap.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

question.leadin: This state gained power thanks to Shang Yang's reforms, and the kingdom of Han instantly surrendered to this kingdom when King An believed they would invade.
question.text: Name this kingdom whose leader Ying Zheng conquered six other states, which began a namesake dynasty.
question.clue: Li Si advised this dynasty's most notable ruler, who eventually died due to mercury poisoning while trying to find the elixir of life.

swap.text: This explorer gave Hassan-i Sabbah the title of "Old Man of the Mountain" and also claimed he surrounded Alamut with rivers of milk and honey. This Italian more famously served in the court of Kublai Khan.
swap.clue: After he was captured by the Genoese, a participant described this event to prison-mate Rustichello.

question.leadin: Nazi Party member John Rabe tried to stop this event and protected thousands of people during it.
question.text: Name this event. The controversy surrounding Iris Chang's book on this event may have been a factor in her 2004 suicide.
question.answerHtml: Nanking massacre [or Nanjing massacre; or Rape of Nanking; or Rape of Nanjing]

swap.leadin: The Yan Dynasty he created collapsed soon after his assassination by his son.
swap.text: Identify this angry Soghdian diaper enthusiast who started the destructive Anshi revolt in 755 CE, which was initially targeted towards then-Chancellor Yang Guozhong.
swap.clue: This man lost the Battle of Yongqiu after his general was baited into retreating 30 miles from the fortress by Zhang Xun.

question.leadin: The Mongol invasion of China subjugated this northern kingdom whose own invasion of China had led to the formation of the Southern Song.
question.text: Name this dynasty founded by the Jurchens, whose name literally means "gold" in Chinese.
question.clue: The next masters of the northern Chinese frontier were this dynasty, which overthrew the Liao and ruled from 1115 to 1234, when their capital of Kaifeng fell. They banned all Chinese culture from their army in an attempt to preserve their ethnic identity.

swap.leadin: Many courtesans were trained at a performing arts academy in this city nicknamed "the Pear Garden."
swap.text: Name this city, where an imperial consort held a comic ceremony whereby she wrapped a general in a large silk diaper. This city also contains the Great Wild Goose Pagoda.
swap.answerHtml: Xi’an (“shee-AHN”) [or Chang’an] (Yang Guifei wrapped An Lushan in a diaper.)
swap.clue: The Silk Road had its eastern origin in this city, where Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi was buried with his Terracotta Army.

question.leadin: In a battle named for this location, Charles Elliot ordered British ships to fire on Chinese junks enforcing a food sale embargo that had been triggered by a deadly bar fight, thus beginning the First Opium War.
question.text: Identify this location that is often said to include a namesake peninsula. The 14K ("fourteen-K") organization enjoyed near-autonomy in a neighborhood named for this location that was demolished in the 1990s.
question.answerHtml: Kowloon [or Gáulùhng or Jǐulóng; accept Kowloon Peninsula or Kowloon Walled City]

swap.text: This Tang princess was married off to Songtsen Gampo, the founder of the Tibetan Empire. She is traditionally credited with introducing Chinese agriculture, porcelain, and other innovations to Tibetan culture.
